evals.prompt: I have a Java service that makes 3 API calls and I want them to run in parallel. What's the modern Java 21 way to do this?
evals.expected_output: On a stock Java 21, virtual threads are the stable primitive: submit the calls to Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor(), collect the Futures, and cancel the siblings yourself if one fails. StructuredTaskScope is a preview API — it needs an exact JDK pin plus --enable-preview at compile and runtime, and its API changed between previews, so recommend it only when the project opts in.

assertions.description: Pairs StructuredTaskScope with its preview status across a sentence
Rejects claiming the preview API is stable in Java 21
Rejects claiming it is the default API in Java 21
assertions.value: StructuredTaskScope is the default in Java 21

evals.prompt: My Java REST server handles thousands of concurrent requests. Should I use a thread pool or Virtual Threads?
evals.expected_output: Use Virtual Threads — Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor(). They're lightweight (cheap to create, cheap to block), ideal for I/O-bound workloads. Do NOT pool them — just create one per task.

evals.prompt: I'm using synchronized blocks with blocking I/O inside a Java Virtual Thread app. My colleague says this is a problem. Why?
evals.expected_output: On JDK 21–23 a virtual thread that blocks inside a synchronized monitor pins its carrier thread, which defeats the point of virtual threads; JEP 491 in JDK 24 removes monitor pinning, so the same code is fine there. Use ReentrantLock when you need timed, interruptible or fair locking, and measure before claiming a performance problem.
